Subject: Recap + ask: POC success criteria, capacity ask, timeline

Hi Alicia / Tom — thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap and a proposed ops/capacity approach so we can lock the POC SOW and timelines. Please confirm or flag changes.

Call recap (agreed):
- Success criteria: (1) 95th %-ile generation latency <= 250ms at expected load; (2) end-to-end quality: Rouge/BLEU-style eval + 5 key business prompts hitting thresholds you provided; (3) integration with your filtering pipeline with <1% post-filter drop rate.
- Evaluation plan: 2-week smoke test (end-to-end) followed by a 4-week evaluation window with real traffic sampling.
- Ownership: Luma product (Alicia) will validate quality, Redwood SE (Monica) will run performance and infra, Hannah will coordinate timelines and billing, procurement (Tom) will own SOW/PO.

Capacity ask (initial proposal):
- Reserved baseline: 3 x 80GB A100-equivalent GPUs to guarantee steady-state concurrency for synchronous calls (model: open-variant you mentioned).
- Burst policy: autoscale up to 9 GPUs for short peaks (queue-based scale up, 5-minute cool-down).
- Caching: prefix and KV cache for session continuity — expect ~35-45% token cost reduction for repeated prompts.
- Target monitoring: token-level cost breakdown and 95th %-ile latency dashboards; automated fallback to smaller quantized variant when latency breach >3 minutes.

Attached: draft POC_SOW_v1.pdf and resource_estimate.xlsx with rough cost-hours.

Proposed timeline:
- Week 1: SOW sign and infra provisioning (reserved capacity allocation)
- Week 2: Integration + smoke tests
- Weeks 3-6: Evaluation, metrics collection, and final review

Please confirm the success criteria above and whether the baseline/burst GPU sizing aligns with your expected peak QPS (you mentioned ~2.2k peak QPS during demos). If you agree, Monica and I will produce a tightened resource estimate and a final SOW for procurement.

Thanks,

Hi Alicia / Hannah — I scoped the capacity and ops plan based on your QPS estimates and dataset notes. Summary and concrete asks below.

1) Baseline reservation (guaranteed):
- 3 x 80GB A100-class vGPUs (reserved for the duration of the 6-week POC). This supports ~1.1k sustained QPS with latency buffer for your model size and prompt lengths (averaging ~450 tokens per request).

2) Autoscaling / burst policy:
- Scale out triggers: queue length > 12 or CPU < 20% on worker nodes for 90s OR average latency > 200ms for 30s.
- Burst cap: automatic scale to 9 GPUs for short bursts (max burst = 30 minutes in a 2-hour window) unless manual approval is granted.
- Cost guardrail: notify procurement and pause automated bursts if projected hourly spend exceeds the soft cap we list in the SOW.

3) Caching & batching approach:
- Continuous batching for synchronous calls with max batch window 30ms.
- KV + prefix caching (session stickiness at user-id) — expect cache hit 35-45% and 30% token savings based on prompt reuse you've described.

4) Networking & infra asks (from your note):
- Recommendation: AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering for reduced variance — we can support both. Expect additional setup time of 2-3 business days.

5) Monitoring, rollback, and SLOs:
- Dashboards: 95th/99th latency, token cost per route, GPU utilization per host, error rates.
- Auto-fallback: if latency SLO violated for >3 consecutive minutes, route to quantized model variant; if quality regressions triggered by your eval set, rollback to previous model version.

6) Cost estimate (rough):
- Reserved baseline (3 x 80GB A100) ~ $X/hr (see attached resource_estimate.xlsx, tab: capacity_rundown).
- Peak hourly rate (9 GPUs) ~ $Y/hr. We’ll include a soft spend cap and an alerting workflow in the SOW.

Next steps I propose:
- Hannah: confirm business approval for baseline and burst caps (Aditya if you want to review cost thresholds).
- Alicia/Tom: confirm procurement guardrail number (target $/hr cap).
- Monica: finalize network requirements doc and update resource_estimate.xlsx; produce an updated SOW draft with burst policy language.

Attaching updated resource_estimate.xlsx and network_requirements.docx (stubs).

Cheers,
